bgm_list: Oriental Enlightened Autumn Opera

Title screen theme.

This theme is nothing new; this is an arrangement of the title screen theme from a canceled Emiverse project.
The original premise involved a beast, but there is no beast in this game.
How would Hosokawa-san react if I made this game into an Emiverse game?
This is a canon entry to the Drillimation Danmaku Universe, so...
Beginning of the Search for a Rumor

Stage 1 theme.

Where do I begin? Every first stage should evoke a "beginning" feel where you are out searching for any secrets that could make a huge impact.
I wrote this in E major so I could get that "autumn" feel.
Of course, this would be a theme to play on your way to school after the summer break ends. ^^;
Little Tengu Courier

Kotori Tegami's theme.

She is a tengu mail courier who often loses the mail she is tasked with delivering. It spreads everywhere she goes and forces the passerby to pick it up.
The note volume and fast tempo is meant to illustrate this scramble. I went my way of making it a rockin' track, as with every boss in the game.
A Million Secrets That No One Knows ~ Mayohiga Punch

Stage 2 theme.

What is there I have to say? Mayohiga has only appeared in the first Mythos of Phantasmagoria so far, and this game marks the second.
I sort of envisioned it as an autumn version of The Fantastic Tales of Tohno from Perfect Cherry Blossom.
It still kind of sounds like the original but interpolated. ^^;
The Morning Ritual of the Kitsune Shrine Maiden

Koko Akashita's theme.

We've seen a youkai shrine maiden before, perhaps Yumi Ochiai maybe?
Reimu is questioning how a shrine in Mayohiga showed up. She will definitely have some serious competition. ^^;
I describe this theme as "traditional Japanese jazz", though I didn't emphasize the jazzy part much, and I still kept some metal-sounding parts.
The Midnight Crossing of the Tanuki

Ritsuu Midoriue's theme.

The boss is a tanuki, I took Mamizou's theme and reimagined it as an early game boss theme.
Ritsuu is one of those characters who dresses more masculine unlike her feminine counterpart.
My next project may feature a similar character. ^^;
Hiking Through the Amber Woods ~ Whispers of the Golden Equinox

Stage 3 theme.

I composed this theme on a boring Sunday morning when I had nothing to do.
This theme follows the journey from Tohno to Yumemura, through a new location called the Amber Woods.
There isn't anything nostalgic to fit this tune; it just illustrates the adventurous and brisk stroll through the woods.
In the motifs leading up to the key changes, I made the chord progressions in each second bar dissonant to symbolize the air beginning to rot.
I needed some fresher afternoon air after that. ^^;
The Day Leaves Magically Turn Yellow ~ Autumn's Formal Arrival
Dream Village ~ Tengu's Den

Stage 4 theme.

This is just an arrangement of the theme of the same name from the second Mythos of Phantasmagoria.
It's been expanded and sped up in tempo to fit a standard stage theme. The major differences I included are having low chord progressions to illustrate you getting closer to a glohmed person.
You'll never know what could be inside. ^^;
The Serpentine Calamitosus Befalling You

Ryuuko and Saika's theme.

This is an arrangement of the Tatsumaru sisters' battle theme, also from the second Mythos of Phantasmagoria game.
The original had two separate versions, and I've combined both of them into one theme.
The only difference is giving the boss fight more of a metal feel, as illustrated by the distortion guitar.
I don't know if it will make the sisters slither any faster. ^^;
The Labyrinth of Silent Dust ~ Floor of a Fading Dream

Stage 5 theme.

It seems to be a common trend with the two previous fangames I've made: four stages outside, last two inside.
It's the third time I've done this. ^^;
Anyway, since this is a mansion, I wanted it to sound stagnant yet regal.
The curse on Fusana makes it feel like time had stopped. She doesn't have the ability to stop time unlike Sakuya.
The versal parts are repetitive to simulate the feeling of navigating hallways that look identical. Then it breaks when you encounter Fusana, and the environment becomes grander and more royal.
The Daytime Maid Who Becomes a Princess at Sunset

Fusana Midorigawa's theme.

Having to compose separate day and night counterparts for every single character would be cumbersome. I merged her maid and princess aspects into one entire theme.
The intro and verse are meant to reflect her daytime occupation, while the waltz section reflects her nighttime transition.
Given that the all the boss themes are inspired by visual kei, this ended up being an orchestral rock mix.
Out of everything I could think of, this is the longest stage 5 boss theme I've composed in my career. ^^;
Threshold of Scarlet Despair ~ Silent Manor's Echo

Final stage theme.

I don't know why this theme sounds more for a boss instead of a stage. ^^;
I ended up leaning into metal for this track like what I've done for all boss themes in this game.
The pipe organ used in most of the track reflects the visual kei feel of the game's final bosses. They also reflect the "echo" the player has now made inside the manor.
You already know what despair lies inside.
The Housemaid Invader Sweeping the Gloom and Doom

Berenice Grieg's theme.

Visual kei was a major focus for this theme. I did a mix of heavy metal and synth instruments, and it seemed to work well.
Man, is she mad here? Her next goal is to place glohm on you.
She used it to have Fusana join the Gensokyo Socialite Order, an organization you have no plans to join.
Who's next?
Shattered Dust ~ The Twin Maid's Severe Retaliation

Veronica Grieg's theme.

I've had games where there's more than one final boss theme. My previous game had three, and this one has two.
When something gets another final boss theme, you expect things to be darker than the first.
The first half of it starts light for Veronica to prepare her revenge on you, and the second really shows her power.
This song really has a final-sounding melody throughout.
Nearly a Year After Vladrouge's Defeat

Extra stage theme.

When I thought about setting the stage in the Scarlet Devil Mansion, I wondered if it was going to be a duplicate of Embodiment of Scarlet Devil.
Not nearly identical, despite this being an arrangement of said game's extra stage theme.
You see, I knew Flandre wouldn't be the extra stage boss, so I swapped it for another member of the Scarlet family.
I also arranged "Demonic Place" from Immaterial and Missing Power for color.
The Desire to End All of the Sorcerer's Miseries

Camille Scarlet's theme.

First, it started as a fan theme for a cancelled Studio Emiko VTuber project.
Then it became the Elite Four battle theme for the second Mythos of Phantasmagoria game.
And now, it has become the theme of Camille Scarlet, the mother of the Scarlet sisters.
Arranging this theme was more of a copypaste job. ^^;
The Great Autumn Festival ~ Parallel World's End

Phantasm stage theme.

When you hear the word "phantasm", you think of a stage that's even harder than extra.
You expect the music to swell up. Instead of arranging the extra stage theme to have more flair, I simply arranged the extra stage theme from the second Chuhou Joutai game.
I shifted the key to a minor one to ensure it fit within the autumn atmosphere, and it really shows its oriental potential.
Gensokyo's Evening Bell ~ Twilight of the Socialite Order

Doromi Akatsuki's theme.

This is how a Phantasm stage boss theme should sound like. If all you did was arrange an existing theme like in Perfect Cherry Blossom, the boss's identity won't be unique.
My aim was to differentiate Doromi from Camille by making sure it represented the game's true finale.
Making it dark and epic helped ensure that a very tough opponent is in front of you.
Nothing else is needed for explanation. ^^;
Departure in an Autumn Breeze

Ending theme.

Where do I begin? I originally composed this for Marvelous Faceless Reflection, like the first three songs in the game's sountrack.
I envisioned this as an autumn version of Dream of a Spring Breeze from Perfect Cherry Blossom.
This is no doubt the longest ending theme I ever composed. Most of them seem to be a minute or two in length but how did that double!? ^^;
There may be no answer to this.
The October Sky's Gentle Reflection

Staff roll theme.

At first, I originally wanted to go entirely original, before this became a credits medley. Aside from original stuff, I arranged Kotori and Fusana's themes into it.
This whole thing is in 6/4 time to explain the relationship between Fusana and her partner.
As a way to explain this bittersweet victory, I made it conclusive yet nostalgic, expanding the autumn breeze of the ending theme.
Interestingly, this was composed in the spring. ^^;
Player's Score

Name entry theme.

This is the same old song that I have been arranging since Song of Divine Tempest.
The instruments remain the same, but it sounds entirely different.
Every time I arrange it, it feels like a copypaste job.
Next time I arrange it, I'll promise to change things up.
